questions.question: A freely suspended magnet always aligns in the ________direction.
questions.solution:
A **freely suspended magnet** always aligns in the **__North-South__** direction.

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• **Bar magnet**: A bar magnet is a rectangular piece of the object which is having two poles north and south pole, when suspended freely aligns along the earth's magnetic field north pole, will be pointing towards the magnetic north pole of the earth.
 
• Earth's magnetism is due to the magnetic effect of current which is flowing in the liquid core at the centre of the Earth.
 
 
• Earth is a huge electromagnet. Permanent magnets cannot exits above 650 celsius.
 
 

**EXPLANATION**__:

 
• A **freely suspended magnet** does not show exact geographical South and North because the magnetic axis and geographical axis of the Earth do not coincide.
 
• **Earth** itself behaves as a **magnet **which causes a **freely suspended magnet (or magnetic needle)** to point always in a particular direction: **North and South. **So option 1 is correct.
 
• The **South Pole of the Earth's magnet** is in the geographical North because it attracts the **North Pole** of the suspended magnet and vice versa.

questions.question: Green leaves make their food by the process of photosynthesis using ________ and water. This happens in the presence of sunlight.
questions.solution:
__

• Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, some bacteria and some protistans use the energy from sunlight to produce glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
 
• This glucose can be converted into pyruvate which releases adenosine triphosphate (ATP) by cellular respiration.
 
• The conversion of usable sunlight energy into chemical energy is associated with the action of the green pigment chlorophyll.
 
• Chlorophyll a absorbs its energy from the violet-blue and reddish orange-red wavelengths, and little from the intermediate (green-yellow-orange) wavelengths.

questions.question: Butter Paper is an example of ________ object.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**translucent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Butter Paper** is an example of a **translucent object**.
 
• A **translucent object** allows some amount of light to pass through it, but not entirely. This property makes objects behind it appear **blurry** or unclear.
 
• Butter paper is widely used in **baking and cooking** to prevent food from sticking, as well as in **arts and crafts** for tracing purposes.
 
• Examples of other **translucent materials** include **frosted glass, wax paper, and thin plastic sheets.**
 
• The property of being translucent lies between **opaque** (which does not allow light to pass) and **transparent** (which allows light to pass completely).
 
• In scientific terms, **translucency** is a material characteristic where light is scattered as it passes through the object, preventing the formation of a clear image on the other side.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Opaque**__

 __
 
• **Opaque objects** do not allow light to pass through. As a result, no image is visible through them.
 
• Examples of opaque materials include **wood, metal, and stone.**
 
 
 
• **Luminous**__
 __
 
• **Luminous objects** are those that emit their own light.
 
• Examples include the **sun, stars, and electric bulbs.**
 
 
 
• **Transparent**__
 
 
• **Transparent objects** allow light to pass through completely, making objects on the other side clearly visible.
 
• Examples include **clear glass, clean water, and thin air.**
